# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment

The baseline passes the supplied simulation, uses 15 LUTs and 6 FFs, and has setup WNS −0.946 ns with hold WHS +0.167 ns, so timing closure is the first objective. The reported critical path runs from `read_ptr` through distributed RAM selection to `out_last`; the advisor indicates pad and clock insertion delay dominate, so changing pointer logic alone is unlikely to close it.

## Hypothesis

Registering the FIFO head tuple and driving `out_data` and `out_last` directly from those registers should remove the RAM read selection from the output path and may improve routed setup slack, at the cost of additional FFs and possibly LUTs.

## Instruction for generator

Replace the asynchronous `data_mem[read_ptr]` and `last_mem[read_ptr]` output selection with a registered head tuple and shift-register tail storage, so both payload outputs are driven directly by the head registers. Capture a push into the head when empty; on a pop, promote the next queued tuple and correctly compact or append the tail when push and pop coincide. Preserve the existing capacity, ready/valid behavior, reset priority, stall stability, minimum transfer age, parameter support, and top `// @latency 1` annotation; expect FF use to rise and treat timing recovery as unproven until all gates and routed reports pass.
